lesson.intro: El estilo indirecto (reported speech) sirve para contar lo que alguien dijo sin repetirlo textualmente. Cuatro cosas suelen cambiar: el tiempo verbal (backshift, porque said/told va en pasado), los pronombres, las palabras de tiempo y lugar, y el orden en las preguntas (sin inversion, sin do).

sections.heading: 1 - Reported statements
sections.body:
Estructura: say / tell (+ persona) + (that) + oracion. El that es opcional.

Como el verbo introductor suele ir en pasado (said, told), el verbo de dentro retrocede un tiempo (backshift).
examples: "I'm tired." → He said (that) he was tired.
"We live here." → They said they lived there.
"I passed!" → She said she had passed.

sections.heading: 2 - El backshift de tiempos verbales
sections.body:
Con said / told en pasado:

  • presente simple → pasado simple
  • presente continuo → pasado continuo
  • presente perfect / pasado simple → past perfect
  • will → would; can → could; may → might; must (obligacion) → had to

No cambian: would, could, might, should. No se hace backshift si el verbo introductor esta en presente (She says...) o si es una verdad general todavia valida.
examples: "I saw her." → He said he had seen her.
"I can drive." → She said she could drive.
The teacher said that water boils at 100 °C. (verdad general)

sections.heading: 3 - Reported questions
sections.body:
Sin inversion: el orden es el de una oracion afirmativa (sujeto + verbo). Se quita el auxiliar do/does/did y el signo de interrogacion.

  • Preguntas de si/no → if / whether.
  • Preguntas con wh- → se mantiene la palabra wh-.

Verbo introductor: ask (+ objeto opcional).
examples: "Where do you live?" → She asked where I lived.
"Are you OK?" → He asked if I was OK.
"What time is it?" → She asked what time it was.

sections.heading: 4 - Reported commands and requests
sections.body:
tell / ask + objeto (me, him...) + (not) to + infinitivo.

Ordenes → tell; peticiones educadas → ask. La negativa: not to + infinitivo. say no se usa para ordenes.
examples: "Sit down." → She told me to sit down.
"Don't touch it." → He told me not to touch it.
"Please wait." → She asked me to wait.

sections.heading: 5 - Cambios de tiempo y lugar
sections.body:
now → then; today → that day; tonight → that night; tomorrow → the next / following day; yesterday → the day before / the previous day; ... ago → ... before; next week → the following week; here → there; this → that; these → those.

Solo se cambian si el contexto (momento o lugar) ya no es el mismo.
examples: "I'll call you tomorrow." → He said he'd call me the next day.
"I saw it here yesterday." → She said she'd seen it there the day before.
"I'm busy now." → He said he was busy then.

sections.heading: 6 - say vs tell y otros verbos
sections.body:
tell va seguido de una persona (tell me, tell him). say no (say that..., o say to me).

Otros verbos: explain (that), admit / deny + -ing, suggest / recommend + -ing o that, promise / offer / refuse + to, remind sb to, warn sb (not) to.

Expresiones fijas: tell the truth / a lie / a story / the time; say hello / sorry / a few words.
examples: She told me the news.
She said that she was tired.
He admitted breaking the vase.
She promised to help.

sections.heading: 7 - Cambios de pronombres
sections.body:
Los pronombres y posesivos cambian segun quien habla y de quien se habla ahora.

I del que hablaba → he / she; you → segun a quien se dirigia; my / your → his / her / my... El truco: piensa quien dice la frase reportada y a quien.
examples: Ana a mi: "I like your car." → Ana said she liked my car.
Tom a Ana: "I'll help you." (Ana lo cuenta) → Tom said he'd help me.
Ana: "My brother lives here." → Ana said her brother lived there.

sections.heading: 8 - Transformar a estilo indirecto
sections.body:
Pasos:

  1. Elige say / tell / ask (+ persona).
  2. Haz el backshift del verbo si said esta en pasado.
  3. Cambia pronombres y posesivos.
  4. Cambia palabras de tiempo / lugar si hace falta.
  5. En preguntas: orden de afirmativa, sin do, con if para si/no. En ordenes: (not) to + infinitivo.
examples: "I am busy." → He said he was busy.
"Do you smoke?" → She asked if I smoked.
"Call me later." → He told me to call him later.

mistakes: NO: She said me that she was tired. -> SI: She told me / She said that she was tired.
NO: He asked me where did I live. -> SI: He asked me where I lived.
NO: He told me that sit down. -> SI: He told me to sit down.
NO: She said she will come. -> SI: She said she would come.
NO: He asked that I was ready. -> SI: He asked if / whether I was ready.
NO: They told to me the news. -> SI: They told me the news.
NO: She said me to wait. -> SI: She told / asked me to wait.

questions.prompt: 'I'm tired.' -> She said (that) she ___ tired.
'We live in Rome.' -> They said they ___ in Rome.
El 'that' tras say / tell es:
'I passed!' -> He said he ___.
'She works hard.' -> He told me she ___ hard.

questions.explanation: Porque el verbo introductor va en pasado.

questions.prompt: 'I don't like coffee.' -> He said he ___ (not like) coffee.
questions.explanation: don't -> didn't (backshift de presente a pasado).

questions.prompt: 'It will rain.' -> The forecast said it ___ rain.
'I can swim.' -> She said she ___ swim.
'They have arrived.' -> He said they ___.
'said' esta en ___, y por eso hay backshift.
questions.explanation: El verbo introductor en pasado arrastra el resto al pasado.

options: el auxiliar 'do/does/did' y el signo de interrogacion
questions.answer: el auxiliar 'do/does/did' y el signo de interrogacion

questions.prompt: 'Why are you late?' -> She asked me why I ___ (be) late.
'Can you help?' -> He asked if I ___ help.
Cual es correcta?
options: She asked where the station was.
She asked where was the station.
She asked where the station is?
questions.answer: She asked where the station was.
questions.explanation: Sin inversion, sin signo de interrogacion, con backshift.

questions.prompt: 'Have you finished?' -> She asked if I ___ finished.
El verbo para reportar una pregunta suele ser:
'Who called?' -> He wanted to know who ___.
questions.explanation: Backshift; en preguntas de sujeto se mantiene el orden.

questions.prompt: 'When does the shop open?' -> I asked when the shop ___.
'Sit down.' -> She told me ___ down.
'Don't touch it!' -> He told me ___ it.
Reported command = tell/ask + ___ + (not) to + infinitivo.
questions.explanation: Siempre lleva la persona: told me, asked him...

questions.prompt: 'Please wait here.' -> She asked me ___ there.
'Be quiet!' -> The teacher told us ___ quiet.
Para ordenes usamos ___; para peticiones educadas, ___.
questions.explanation: tell me to... (orden) / ask me to... (peticion).

questions.prompt: 'Open the window.' -> He told me ___ (open) the window.
'Don't be late.' -> She reminded me ___ late.
Cual es correcta?
options: He told me to call him.
He said me to call him.
questions.answer: He told me to call him.
questions.explanation: tell necesita objeto; say no se usa para ordenes.

questions.prompt: 'I'll be there at 6.' (reportado el mismo dia) -> She said she'd be there at 6.
questions.explanation: Si el plan sigue en pie, no hay que cambiar la hora.
